synopsis: NASA-STD-7009B was approved on 5 March 2024 and establishes modeling and simulation practice around credibility, verification, validation, sensitivity and uncertainty [f9737, f10599]. It assesses credibility across development and use, ties credibility effort to the consequences of a wrong decision, and, alongside ASME V&V 40, retains physical testing where decision risk is high or validation evidence is weakest [f9739, f9738, f7834, f7835]. Programs must define acceptance criteria, obtain technical-authority approval, and disclose dissenting technical opinions with results [f9539, f10600, f9741]. The planning chapter recommends credibility frameworks such as NASA-STD-7009B instead of TRLs for the collision-mitigation validation toolchain; blind-prediction gaps support this choice, although the frameworks are described as largely declarative [f9536, f10031, f10028, f10029]. An assessor-quality package requires more than simulator results, with recommended plan sections of 2–6 pages for evidence, V&V and test strategy, 1–1.5 pages for credibility and tool qualification, and 1–2 pages for results and review protocol [f8026, f10162, f10164, f10178].
